add-016.title: Strawberry Banana Smoothie
add-016.culturalNotes: Using frozen strawberries or banana gives a thick, cold smoothie without ice that dilutes the flavour. Add a spoon of chia seeds or oats for a quick breakfast.

instructions.1: Wash and hull the strawberries and slice the banana.
instructions.2: Put the fruit in the blender with the milk, honey, yogurt and ice.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth and creamy, pour into glasses and serve at once.

add-017.title: Herb-Roasted Potatoes with Tahini-Yogurt Sauce
add-017.culturalNotes: Covering the potatoes at first steams them through, then uncovering under the grill gives a crisp crust without much oil.

add-017-i5.name: Paprika, ground coriander and dried thyme

add-017-i10.name: Grated garlic and cumin for the sauce

add-017-i11.name: Parsley or fresh coriander to garnish

instructions.1: Peel the potatoes, cut into medium cubes or wedges and toss in a bowl with the olive oil, garlic, spices and salt until coated.
instructions.2: Spread in a tray side by side, cover with baking paper then foil, and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.
instructions.3: Uncover and brown the potatoes under the grill until golden and crisp.
instructions.4: Mix the tahini, yogurt, water, vinegar, garlic, cumin and salt until creamy.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the potatoes with parsley and serve with the tahini-yogurt sauce.

add-018.title: Basbousa Stuffed with Ashta Cream
add-018.culturalNotes: Cream cheese and labneh with cornflour make a stable ashta that does not run when cut; you can use ready-made fresh ashta if available.

add-018-i5.name: Butter, ghee or a ghee-oil mix

add-018-i11.name: For the ashta: unsalted cream cheese

add-018-i13.name: For the ashta: sugar and vanilla

add-018-i14.name: Syrup: sugar, water and lemon
add-018-i14.standardAmount: 1 cup sugar + ¾ cup water + lemon slices

instructions.1: Mix the semolina, sugar, coconut and baking powder, add the fat and stir until the semolina is coated; rest 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the canned cream, then the eggs and milk, and fold gently until even.
instructions.3: Spread half the mixture 1 cm thick in a greased tin and bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until the edges brown.
instructions.4: For the ashta: stir the cold milk with the cornflour and sugar over heat until thick, remove, add the vanilla, cream cheese and labneh, mix and let cool 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Spread the ashta over the baked layer and let it set 15 minutes, then spoon the rest of the basbousa mixture over the top.
instructions.6: Return to the oven at 190°C for 15 minutes until the top is golden.
instructions.7: Pour the hot syrup over as soon as it comes out, cover, leave an hour, then chill an hour before cutting.

add-019.title: Egyptian Sobia with Homemade Mix
add-019.culturalNotes: Sobia is a popular Ramadan drink in Egypt, originally made from rice or coconut soaked in milk. The homemade mix makes dozens of glasses and keeps two months in a dry place.

add-019-i9.name: To serve: banana, mango and strawberries

instructions.1: Grind the coconut to a powder in a spice grinder, mix it with the milk powder, Chantilly powder, starch, sugar and vanilla, and store in an airtight jar.
instructions.2: Cut the fruit and divide it among serving glasses.
instructions.3: Blend the cold water with the sugar and 2 tbsp of the mix on high speed for a full minute until very frothy.
instructions.4: Pour the sobia over the fruit and serve ice-cold.
instructions.5: For classic sobia without fruit: blend the mix with cold milk instead of water and serve with a pinch of cinnamon.

add-020.title: No-Bake Cheesecake
add-020.culturalNotes: The gelatine must dissolve completely before it goes in, or the cream will be grainy. The topping can be swapped for strawberry, caramel or Lotus.

add-020-i9.name: Blueberry sauce or jam for the top

instructions.1: Mix the ground biscuits with the butter until like wet sand, press into the base of a springform tin and chill.
instructions.2: Mash the cheese portions, add the cream cheese, icing sugar and vanilla and beat until smooth.
instructions.3: Add the liquid cream and keep beating until thick.
instructions.4: Dissolve the gelatine completely in the hot water and add it gradually to the cream while beating.
instructions.5: Pour over the base, smooth and chill for at least 3-4 hours until set.
instructions.6: Spread the sauce or jam on top, release the sides of the tin and serve cold.

add-021.title: Yellow Lentil Koshari (Alexandrian Koshari)
add-021.culturalNotes: Yellow koshari is a popular Alexandrian dish, quicker than classic brown-lentil koshari and sometimes called 'white koshari'. It is usually served with fried fish, pickled lemon or tahini.

add-021-i6.name: Black pepper and salt
add-021-i6.standardAmount: 1 tsp pepper + a pinch of salt

instructions.1: For the sauce: fry the garlic in the oil until pale golden, add the tomato juice, cumin, chilli and salt and simmer until thick.
instructions.2: Mix the rice and lentils, wash well and drain.
instructions.3: Melt the ghee in a pot, dissolve the stock cubes in it, add the rice and lentils with the black pepper and stir 2 minutes to coat.
instructions.4: Add the warm water, adjust the salt, boil on high until the water drops, then cover on very low heat for 20 minutes until cooked.
instructions.5: Fluff gently and serve with the hot sauce and crispy onions.

add-022.title: Homemade Turkish-Style Chicken Mortadella
add-022.culturalNotes: The secret to a firm texture is mincing the chicken to a paste and poaching in water that never boils hard, so the log does not crack. Keeps 4-5 days in the fridge or freeze in slices.

add-022-i11.name: Pitted green olives or whole peppercorns (optional)

instructions.1: Process the chicken in a food processor to a very smooth paste, then add the eggs, cornflour, oil, beetroot water, garlic and spices and process again until even.
instructions.2: Fold in the olives or peppercorns with a spoon.
instructions.3: Place the paste on heat-safe cling film or a cooking bag, roll into a very tight log, tie the ends and wrap in foil.
instructions.4: Poach the log in hot, not boiling, water (about 80°C) for 50-60 minutes, turning occasionally.
instructions.5: Transfer straight to iced water for 10 minutes, then chill at least 4 hours before slicing.

add-023.title: Stovetop Cheese Kunafa
add-023.culturalNotes: Cheese kunafa is famous in the Palestinian city of Nablus. If using akkawi or Nabulsi cheese, soak it in water for several hours, changing the water, to remove the salt.

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon, add the vanilla, simmer 10 minutes on low and cool.
instructions.2: Crumble the frozen kunafa by hand or in a processor until fine and rub the melted ghee into it until fully absorbed.
instructions.3: Press half the kunafa into a greased tray, spread the cheese in the middle away from the edges, cover with the rest of the kunafa and press gently.
instructions.4: Set the tray over medium heat and keep turning it until the base browns evenly, about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.5: Invert the kunafa onto a second greased tray and return to the heat until the other side browns and the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over the hot kunafa, sprinkle with pistachios and serve at once while the cheese is hot and stretchy.

add-024.title: Sahlab with Mastic
add-024.culturalNotes: Sahlab was originally made from the powdered tubers of an orchid, and is now prepared with starch and rice flour. For a spoonable sahlab, add an extra teaspoon of starch.

add-024-i8.name: Mastic ground with a spoon of sugar

add-024-i10.name: To garnish: cinnamon, toasted nuts and coconut

instructions.1: Mix all the dry ingredients well and store in an airtight jar in a dry place.
instructions.2: For each cup of milk, dissolve 2 tbsp of the mix completely in the cold milk before heating, so it does not form lumps.
instructions.3: Cook on low heat, whisking constantly, until it thickens and starts to boil.
instructions.4: Pour into cups, garnish with cinnamon, coconut and nuts and serve hot.

add-025.title: Kunafa with Mango and Cream
add-025.culturalNotes: The best mangoes for this dessert are ripe, low-fibre varieties such as Owais or Zebdia. Serve cold on the same day so the kunafa stays crisp.

instructions.1: Crumble the kunafa and rub in the ghee and icing sugar until absorbed.
instructions.2: Press into a tray and bake at 180°C until golden and crisp, or toast it crumbled in a pan on low heat, stirring.
instructions.3: Pour the cold syrup over the hot kunafa and let it cool.
instructions.4: Whip the Chantilly powder with the cold milk and ashta until doubled; you can add 2 tbsp purée to the cream.
instructions.5: Spread the cream over the kunafa, then the mango cubes, drizzle the purée on top and chill an hour before serving.
instructions.6: For individual servings: toast the kunafa crumbled and layer it in cups with the cream and mango.

add-026.title: Pumpkin Jam with Orange
add-026.culturalNotes: Pumpkin makes a clear golden jam that tastes rather like apricot. Macerating the pumpkin in sugar first means no water is needed, so the cubes keep their shape.

instructions.1: Mix the pumpkin cubes with the sugar and leave 2 hours until plenty of liquid comes out.
instructions.2: Transfer the pumpkin with its liquid to a pot and add the orange juice, zest, cinnamon and star anise.
instructions.3: Cook on medium heat, stirring now and then, until the liquid reduces and the jam reaches the desired thickness.
instructions.4: Add the lemon juice five minutes before taking it off the heat.
instructions.5: Remove the cinnamon and star anise, pour the hot jam into sterilised jars, seal and refrigerate after opening.

add-027.title: Chicken Fajitas
add-027.culturalNotes: Fajitas come from the Tex-Mex cooking of southern Texas and are traditionally served sizzling in an iron skillet so everyone wraps their own at the table.

add-027-i6.name: Cumin, paprika, ground coriander and chilli

add-027-i9.name: Red and green peppers, in strips

instructions.1: Butterfly the chicken breasts into medium-thick slices.
instructions.2: Mix the oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, coriander, spices, cornflour and salt, toss the chicken in it, cover and chill 2 hours or overnight.
instructions.3: Brown the chicken in a little oil over medium heat, turn, cover and cook through.
instructions.4: Remove the chicken and stir-fry the vegetables in the same pan on high heat until tender but still crisp.
instructions.5: Slice the chicken into strips, return to the vegetables for a minute and serve hot with tortillas, salsa and yogurt.

add-028.title: Arabic-Style Chicken Shawarma Platter
add-028.culturalNotes: Shawarma arabi is a Levantine way of serving: the wrap is toasted, cut into bite-size pieces and served as a full meal with fries and garlic sauce.

add-028-i8.name: Cardamom, turmeric, ginger, curry, cumin and black pepper

add-028-i12.name: Toum, pickled cucumber and fries to serve

instructions.1: Mix all the marinade ingredients until smooth, toss the chicken in it, cover and chill 1-2 hours.
instructions.2: Heat a little oil in a wide pan on high heat, add the chicken and stir constantly until cooked and browned at the edges.
instructions.3: Spread the saj bread with toum, place chicken and pickles along one edge and roll tightly.
instructions.4: Toast the roll on a saj or dry pan on both sides until the bread is crisp.
instructions.5: Cut each roll into slanted pieces ('arabi' style) and serve on a plate with fries, toum and pickles.

add-029.title: Egg Salad with Nabulsi Cheese
add-029.culturalNotes: A Palestinian breakfast salad; Nabulsi cheese, scented with mahlab and mastic, gives it a distinctive flavour. Halloumi or akkawi can be used instead.

instructions.1: Soak the cheese cubes in warm water for 15-20 minutes to reduce the salt, then drain well.
instructions.2: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and cut into medium pieces so the yolks don't crumble.
instructions.3: Mix the tomato, cucumber, spring onion and mint in a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the eggs and cheese and toss gently.
instructions.5: Whisk the olive oil, lemon, pepper and nigella seeds, pour over the salad and serve at once, without adding salt.

add-030.title: Indian Chicken Biryani
add-030.culturalNotes: The secret of biryani is 'dum' cooking: half-boiled rice over a thick sauce in a sealed pot, so the rice finishes in the steam and absorbs the spices without clumping.

add-030-i2.name: Whole spices for boiling (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, star anise)
add-030-i2.standardAmount: 3 cardamom + 3 cloves + 1 cinnamon stick + 2 bay leaves + 1 star anise

add-030-i6.name: Turmeric, ground coriander, cumin and red chilli

add-030-i10.name: Saffron soaked in warm milk or rose water

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, ground spices, salt and half the coriander and mint for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Boil the rice in plenty of salted water with the whole spices until only 70% cooked and still firm, then drain.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot, add the chicken with its marinade and cook until half done and the sauce thickens.
instructions.4: Scatter half the fried onion and the rest of the herbs over the chicken, spread the rice on top, and sprinkle with the saffron and remaining onion.
instructions.5: Seal the pot tightly (the lid can be sealed with dough) and cook on very low heat for 25-30 minutes ('dum') until the rice steams through.
instructions.6: Gently lift the biryani from the sides so the white and coloured rice and chicken show, and serve with yogurt raita.

add-031.title: Banana Berry Smoothie
add-031.culturalNotes: Putting the liquid in first helps the blades turn easily with frozen fruit. A very ripe banana means no sugar is needed.

instructions.1: Cut the frozen banana into small pieces so it blends easily.
instructions.2: Put the milk in the blender first, then the yogurt, fruit and honey.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth and thick, adding a little milk if too heavy, and serve at once.

add-032.title: Homemade Noodle Dough (No Machine)
add-032.culturalNotes: The stiffer the dough, the chewier the noodles. Air-dry the strips for an hour, then keep two days in the fridge or freeze for a month.

instructions.1: Mix the flour and salt, add the egg, then the water gradually until the dough comes together; it should be slightly stiff, not sticky.
instructions.2: Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, cover and rest 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Roll very thin with a rolling pin on a starch-dusted surface, then fold into layers, dusting starch between them.
instructions.4: Cut into thin, even strips with a knife, then shake them loose and dust with starch so they don't stick.
instructions.5: Boil in water for 3-4 minutes until they float and are cooked, drain, rinse in cold water and use in stir-fries or soups.

add-033.title: Fried Eggs Three Ways
add-033.culturalNotes: Fresh eggs hold their shape in the pan because the white is thicker. Salt after frying, not before, so the yolk doesn't get spotty.

add-033-i4.name: Optional extras: grated cheese, red pepper, spring onion

instructions.1: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with the butter or oil spread across the surface.
instructions.2: Crack each egg into a small bowl first, then slide it gently into the pan so the yolk doesn't break.
instructions.3: Sunny side up: leave the egg without turning until the white is fully set and the yolk runny; covering the pan for a minute sets the top of the white.
instructions.4: Over easy: once the white sets, flip the egg with a spatula for just 30 seconds.
instructions.5: Over hard: leave on the second side 1-2 minutes until the yolk sets.
instructions.6: Season with salt, pepper and extras and serve at once with bread.

add-034.title: Egyptian Layered Feteer Meshaltet
add-034.culturalNotes: Feteer meshaltet is one of the best-known breads of rural Egypt, traditionally baked in a clay oven. The secret is an elastic dough and many ghee-brushed layers that separate after baking.

add-034-i5.name: Butter or liquid ghee for stretching

add-034-i6.name: Oil to cover the dough balls

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and sugar, add the water gradually and knead into a very soft, smooth, non-sticky dough, then knead 10 minutes more.
instructions.2: Divide into 6-8 balls, submerge them in a tray of oil, cover and rest 30 minutes until relaxed.
instructions.3: Stretch each ball with your fingertips on a ghee-greased surface until paper-thin and translucent, and brush with ghee.
instructions.4: Fold the sheet into a square envelope, stretch a second ball and place the folded square in its centre and fold over; repeat until a pie of 3-4 balls is formed.
instructions.5: Place the pie in a greased tray, press it out with your fingertips to fill the tray, brush with ghee and bake at 220°C for 30-40 minutes until golden and puffed.
instructions.6: Brush with ghee straight out of the oven and clap the edges between your palms to separate the layers; serve with black honey (molasses) and aged cheese or ashta.

add-035.title: Green Olive Pickle
add-035.culturalNotes: Changing the water daily draws out the olives' bitterness. The traditional salt test: a raw egg should float in the brine with a coin-sized patch showing.

instructions.1: Wash the olives and cut one or two slits in each, or crack lightly with a stone without breaking the pit.
instructions.2: Soak in plain water, changing it daily for 7-10 days until the bitterness is gone (taste one to check).
instructions.3: Boil the water with the salt and let it cool completely to make the brine, then add the vinegar.
instructions.4: Pack the olives into a sterilised jar with the lemon, chillies and garlic and cover completely with the brine.
instructions.5: Top with a thin layer of olive oil, close the jar and leave two weeks in a cool place before eating.

add-036.title: Qatayef Asafiri with Ashta
add-036.culturalNotes: They are called 'asafiri' (little birds) for their small size. The bicarbonate goes in at the last moment because it is what opens the holes instantly on the hot griddle.

add-036-i5.name: Baking powder and bicarbonate of soda

add-036-i8.name: Fresh ashta or thick clotted cream

add-036-i11.name: Syrup scented with rose and orange-blossom water

instructions.1: Blend the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder and orange-blossom water with the warm water until smooth and pourable like cream.
instructions.2: Leave 15 minutes until bubbles appear, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
instructions.3: Heat a griddle or non-stick pan well without oil and pour small rounds (the size of a child's palm) with a small spoon.
instructions.4: Cook on one side only until full of holes, the top dries and the bottom colours, then lift and cover with a cloth so they don't dry.
instructions.5: Pinch each round halfway closed into a cone, leaving the opening, and press the edges to stick.
instructions.6: Fill the openings with ashta, dip the tips in pistachio, garnish with orange blossom and serve cold with syrup on the side.

add-037.title: Levantine Trotter (Kawareh) Soup
add-037.culturalNotes: Trotters are rich in natural gelatine and give a thick, glossy broth. Cleaning with flour and lemon and blanching first are the secrets to a clean, odour-free broth.

add-037-i2.name: For cleaning: flour, coarse salt, lemon juice and vinegar
add-037-i2.standardAmount: ½ cup flour + 3 tbsp salt + 2 lemons + 3 tbsp vinegar

add-037-i6.name: Bay leaves, cloves and black peppercorns

instructions.1: Scrub the trotters well with the flour, coarse salt, lemon and vinegar, leave 15 minutes, then rinse under running water.
instructions.2: Blanch for 10 minutes in boiling water and discard the water and scum.
instructions.3: Cover with fresh water, add the onion, whole spices and mastic and simmer gently 3-4 hours (or 1½ hours in a pressure cooker) until the meat falls off the bone and the broth is sticky.
instructions.4: Strain the broth, pull the meat and cartilage from the bones, chop and return to the broth, adjusting the salt.
instructions.5: Fry the garlic in the ghee with the coriander until golden, deglaze with the lemon juice and pour over the soup before serving.

add-038.title: Creamy Seafood Soup
add-038.culturalNotes: The seafood goes in last because it cooks in minutes and turns rubbery if left too long on the heat.

add-038-i12.name: Chopped parsley and lemon to serve

instructions.1: Melt the butter and sauté the onion, celery and carrot until soft, then add the garlic for a minute.
instructions.2: Sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute until the raw smell is gone.
instructions.3: Add the stock gradually, stirring so it doesn't lump, then the spices and bay leaf, and simmer 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
instructions.4: Add the seafood and cook just 3-5 minutes until the shrimp turn pink and everything is cooked but not rubbery.
instructions.5: Stir in the cream, adjust the salt and pepper, heat without boiling and serve sprinkled with parsley, with lemon.

add-039.title: Kofta Dawood Basha
add-039.culturalNotes: The dish is attributed to Dawood Pasha, an Ottoman governor of Baghdad or Egypt, and is one of the meatballs-in-sauce dishes known across Egypt, the Levant and Iraq.

add-039-i4.name: Seven spice, a pinch of cinnamon and cumin

instructions.1: Knead the meat well with the drained onion, parsley, spices and salt and shape into small walnut-sized balls, pressing a pine nut into each if you like.
instructions.2: Brown the balls in the oil in batches on all sides, then lift out.
instructions.3: Soften the sliced onion in the same oil, add the tomato paste and stir, then the tomato juice, water, pomegranate molasses and salt.
instructions.4: Boil the sauce 10 minutes, return the meatballs and simmer 15-20 minutes until thickened.
instructions.5: You can instead arrange the balls in a tray with potatoes and sauce and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Serve the kofta with vermicelli rice, sprinkled with pine nuts.

add-040.title: Layali Lubnan (Semolina Pudding with Ashta)
add-040.culturalNotes: Layali Lubnan ('Lebanese nights') is a cold Lebanese dessert close to qashtaliya, with a layer of semolina milk pudding and a layer of ashta. It is even better made a day ahead.

instructions.1: Stir the milk, semolina and sugar in a pot over medium heat, adding the mastic ground with a little sugar and the orange-blossom water.
instructions.2: Stir constantly until thick and starting to boil, then keep stirring 3 minutes as it bubbles and remove from the heat.
instructions.3: Pour into a tray about 30 cm and tilt it to level the surface; leave to cool.
instructions.4: Chill 2-3 hours until set.
instructions.5: Spread the ashta over the top, scatter the pistachios and raisins, cut into squares and drizzle with syrup or honey to serve.

add-041.title: Eggless Ammonia Cookies (Baskoot Neshader)
add-041.culturalNotes: Baker's ammonia is the secret of crisp Egyptian Eid cookies; its strong smell evaporates completely during baking. Keep it in a sealed jar because it loses strength in the air.

instructions.1: Blend the sugar, milk, oil, salt and vanilla until the sugar dissolves completely.
instructions.2: Pour into a large bowl, add the custard powder, baking powder, ammonia and vinegar and whisk by hand.
instructions.3: Sift the flour over the mixture and knead by hand a few minutes into a smooth, elastic dough that is easy to shape; cover.
instructions.4: Shape with a cookie press or by hand into fingers and rings and arrange on trays lined with baking paper, spaced apart.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until the bases colour and the edges start to brown, turning on the grill for a minute at the end if you like.
instructions.6: Let the cookies cool completely before storing in airtight tins.

add-042.title: Saudi Lamb Kabsa
add-042.culturalNotes: Adding the salt once the meat has started to cook keeps it tender. Kabsa is usually served with spicy dakkous salsa and laban.

add-042-i1.name: Lamb on the bone, large pieces

add-042-i8.name: Whole spices: pierced dried lime, cinnamon, cardamom, galangal, bay leaf
add-042-i8.standardAmount: 2 limes + 2 cinnamon sticks + 5 cardamom + a piece of galangal + 2 bay leaves

add-042-i9.name: Kabsa spice, black pepper and ground cardamom

add-042-i11.name: Raisins, toasted almonds and lemon slices to garnish

instructions.1: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and sear the meat with the whole spices until it changes colour all over.
instructions.2: Add the onion, then the garlic, and stir until soft, then the tomato paste, tomato and kabsa spice.
instructions.3: Cover the meat with hot water, cover and simmer 60-90 minutes (or 35 minutes in a pressure cooker) until tender, adding the salt in the last half hour.
instructions.4: Lift the meat and brown it under the oven grill; measure the stock to 1½ times the volume of the rice.
instructions.5: Add the drained rice to the boiling stock, cook on high until most is absorbed, then cover on very low heat for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Spread the rice on a platter, arrange the meat on top and garnish with raisins, almonds and lemon slices.

add-043.title: Yogurt-Marinated Chicken Wings
add-043.culturalNotes: Yogurt and milk tenderise the wings, while the citrus and ketchup give a sweet-and-sour taste. They can also be grilled over charcoal.

add-043-i8.name: White or black pepper, paprika and thyme

instructions.1: Wash and dry the wings and cut at the joints if you like.
instructions.2: Mix the yogurt, milk, ketchup, oil, vinegar, lemon, spices and salt, and toss the wings in it well.
instructions.3: Cover and chill at least 2 hours or overnight.
instructions.4: Arrange the wings on a tray lined with baking paper and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes, turning halfway.
instructions.5: Brush with the remaining marinade and brown under the grill 5-10 minutes until crisp.
instructions.6: Serve hot with toum or cheese sauce and fries.

add-044.title: Coleslaw
add-044.culturalNotes: Coleslaw is the classic side for fried chicken and burgers. Chilling before serving softens the cabbage slightly and deepens the dressing.

instructions.1: Shred the cabbage finely and grate the carrot, then mix in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Mix the mayonnaise, yogurt, milk, sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth.
instructions.3: Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss until all the cabbage is coated.
instructions.4: Cover and chill at least 30 minutes before serving so the flavours blend.

add-045.title: Homemade Apple Cider Vinegar
add-045.culturalNotes: The jelly-like layer that forms on top is called the 'mother' and shows the fermentation worked; it can be used to start a new batch faster.

add-045-i3.name: Filtered water
add-045-i3.standardAmount: enough to cover the apples (about 1 litre)

instructions.1: Wash and dry the apples and cut into small cubes, skin and seeds included, and place in a wide glass jar.
instructions.2: Dissolve the sugar or honey in the water and pour over the apples to cover completely; a small plate on top keeps them submerged.
instructions.3: Cover the jar with a cotton cloth secured with a rubber band and leave in a warm, dark place, stirring twice a day.
instructions.4: After 2-3 weeks, when the apples sink to the bottom, strain the liquid, return it to the clean jar and cover with the cloth.
instructions.5: Leave another 4-6 weeks until strongly acidic, then bottle and refrigerate.

add-046.title: Quick Crunchy Cucumber Pickles
add-046.culturalNotes: Pouring hot brine over cold cucumbers speeds up the pickling while keeping them crunchy. Choose small, firm cucumbers with few seeds.

add-046-i7.name: Chilli and coriander seeds or dill (optional)

instructions.1: Wash the cucumbers and cut into rounds or spears, or leave whole if very small.
instructions.2: Pack into a sterilised jar with the garlic, chilli and coriander or dill between the layers.
instructions.3: Dissolve the salt and sugar in the boiling water, then add the vinegar.
instructions.4: Pour the hot brine over the cucumbers to cover completely and close the jar.
instructions.5: Let cool, then refrigerate; ready after 3-4 hours and best after a day. Keeps chilled for two weeks.

add-047.title: Homemade Paprika Powder
add-047.culturalNotes: The peppers must be completely dry and snap, or the powder will clump and spoil. A kilo of peppers gives only about 100 g of powder.

add-047-i1.name: Red peppers (sweet, hot or a mix)

instructions.1: Wash and dry the peppers well, cut into thin strips and remove all the seeds and white ribs.
instructions.2: Spread the strips apart on a lined tray and dry in the oven at the lowest heat (60-80°C) with the door slightly open for 3-4 hours until completely brittle.
instructions.3: Alternatively dry them in direct sun for 5-7 days covered with muslin, bringing them in at night.
instructions.4: Let the strips cool completely, then grind in a spice grinder to a fine powder and sift.
instructions.5: Store in an airtight glass jar away from light and heat.
instructions.6: For smoked paprika: smoke the dried strips for 20 minutes in a closed pot with a charcoal ember before grinding.

add-048.title: Indian Onion Pakora
add-048.culturalNotes: Pakora (or pakoda) is one of India's most popular street snacks. Chickpea flour gives crunch and authentic flavour, and cold water keeps the batter from turning chewy.

add-048-i4.name: Black pepper, ground coriander and cumin

instructions.1: Separate the onion slices with your fingers, mix with the salt and spices and leave 5 minutes to release their juice.
instructions.2: Add the flour, chilli and coriander, then cold water a spoonful at a time until the onion is coated in a thick, clinging batter.
instructions.3: Heat the oil over medium heat and drop in small amounts of the mixture with a spoon or your fingers.
instructions.4: Turn until golden brown and crisp (2-3 minutes) and lift out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.
instructions.5: Serve hot with tamarind sauce or mint yogurt sauce.

add-049.title: Kunafa with Chocolate Sauce
add-049.culturalNotes: The blender chocolate sauce sets like cream thanks to the oil added slowly, just like making mayonnaise, so it does not run during baking.

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon for 10-15 minutes and leave the syrup to cool.
instructions.2: Blend the milk with the cocoa, sugar and vanilla, then pour in the oil gradually through the lid while blending until the sauce thickens like cream; chill.
instructions.3: Crumble the kunafa and rub in the butter and coconut until absorbed.
instructions.4: Press half the kunafa into a greased tray, spread some of the chocolate sauce, cover with the rest of the kunafa and press.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C until golden underneath and then on top.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over the hot kunafa and decorate with the remaining chocolate sauce to serve.

add-050.title: Semolina Maamoul with Dates
add-050.culturalNotes: Resting the semolina with ghee overnight is what gives maamoul its sandy texture that melts in the mouth. Maamoul is a classic Eid sweet across the Levant.

add-050-i7.name: Mastic ground with a little sugar

add-050-i9.name: Ghee or butter for the filling

instructions.1: Mix the fine and medium semolina and rub the warm ghee in between your palms until fully absorbed; cover and leave 12-24 hours.
instructions.2: Knead the date paste with the ghee and cinnamon or cardamom and roll into small balls.
instructions.3: Add the icing sugar, mahlab and mastic to the semolina, then the warm milk gradually, bringing the dough together lightly without kneading.
instructions.4: Take a piece of dough, hollow it with your finger, insert a date ball and close, then press into a maamoul mould and tap out with a clear pattern.
instructions.5: Arrange on an ungreased tray and bake at 200°C with bottom heat for 15 minutes, then top heat for a few minutes until lightly golden.
instructions.6: Let cool completely in the tray as they are fragile when hot, then dust with icing sugar and store in airtight tins.

add-051.title: Turkish Chicken Döner
add-051.culturalNotes: Turkish döner is traditionally roasted on a rotating vertical spit. At home, cooking in small batches over very high heat caramelises the edges in the same way.

add-051-i1.name: Chicken breast and thigh, very thin slices

add-051-i8.name: Salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, oregano and a pinch of cinnamon
add-051-i8.standardAmount: 1 tsp each + a pinch of cinnamon

add-051-i10.name: To serve: pickled cucumber, tomato and sumac onions

add-051-i11.name: For the garlic sauce: garlic, mayonnaise, yogurt and lemon

instructions.1: Mix the yogurt, tomato paste, pepper paste, oil, lemon, garlic and spices and marinate the chicken at least 4 hours or overnight.
instructions.2: Heat a griddle or wide iron pan on very high heat and cook the chicken in small batches until the edges brown, without stewing in its juices.
instructions.3: Mix the garlic sauce ingredients until creamy.
instructions.4: Wipe the bread with a little of the chicken fat left in the pan and warm it for a few seconds.
instructions.5: Spread the bread with garlic sauce, add the chicken, pickles, tomato and sumac onions, roll and serve hot.

add-052.title: Smoked Herring Salad with Tahini
add-052.culturalNotes: Herring salad is a dish of Egypt's Sham el-Nessim spring festival. Soaking the herring in milk for half an hour before cleaning reduces the salt if it is very salty.

instructions.1: Pass the herring over a direct gas flame for a few seconds on each side until the skin cracks, making it easy to peel and bringing out the smoky aroma.
instructions.2: Remove the skin and bones completely and cut the flesh into small cubes, keeping the roe if there is any.
instructions.3: Mix the tomato, cucumber, onion and peppers in a bowl.
instructions.4: Whisk the tahini with the lemon, vinegar and a little water until creamy, then add the oil.
instructions.5: Add the herring to the vegetables, pour over the tahini dressing, toss gently, garnish with dill and serve with baladi bread.

add-053.title: Crispy Stuffed Mumbar (Sausage Casings with Rice)
add-053.culturalNotes: Mumbar is an Eid al-Adha dish in Egypt. Filling the casings only two-thirds full is the key, because the rice doubles in size as it boils.

add-053-i1.name: Mumbar (casings) cleaned with salt, vinegar and lemon

add-053-i3.name: Chopped or squeezed tomatoes without water

add-053-i5.name: Chopped dill, parsley and fresh coriander

add-053-i7.name: Salt, black pepper, cumin, a pinch of dried mint and cinnamon

add-053-i8.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves and cardamom

instructions.1: Turn the casings inside out and scrub with salt, flour, vinegar and lemon, rinsing several times until the smell is gone, then turn them back.
instructions.2: Mix the raw rice with the onion, tomato, herbs, oil and spices without cooking.
instructions.3: Cut the casings to manageable lengths, knot one end, fill with the stuffing through a funnel only two-thirds full as the rice swells, and knot the other end.
instructions.4: Prick the mumbar with a needle in several places so it doesn't burst while boiling.
instructions.5: Boil in water with the onion, bay leaves and cardamom over medium heat for 30-45 minutes until the rice is cooked, then drain and let dry.
instructions.6: Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, or brush with oil and brown under the oven grill.
instructions.7: Cut into slanted pieces and serve hot with lemon.

add-054.title: Fresh Garden Salad with Lemon Dressing
add-054.culturalNotes: Dressing just before serving keeps the lettuce crisp. For a full meal, add grilled chicken, boiled chickpeas or feta.

instructions.1: Wash the vegetables well and dry them, because leftover water dilutes the dressing.
instructions.2: Cut all the vegetables into similar-sized pieces and put in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Whisk the olive oil, lemon, pomegranate molasses, salt and pepper until combined.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over the salad just before serving, toss gently and sprinkle with sumac.

add-055.title: Chocolate Banana Smoothie
add-055.culturalNotes: Frozen banana gives a milkshake-like texture without ice cream. Adjust the cocoa or honey to taste.

instructions.1: Slice the banana and put it in the blender with the cocoa, milk and honey.
instructions.2: Add the peanut butter or yogurt for extra nutrition, and ice for freshness.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth and velvety, pour and serve at once.
